SYN-c3c7198d95.report_text:
SURGICAL PATHOLOGY REPORT (SYNTHETIC; NOT A REAL PATIENT)
Patient: M, age band 60-69 | Report year: 2021

SPECIMEN: Lower lobe of lung, left, lobectomy

FINAL DIAGNOSIS: Histologic type: invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma, predominant pattern acinar; high-grade (solid or micropapillary) patterns 30% (IASLC grade 3); Tumor size: 2.6 cm; Visceral pleural invasion: not identified; Margins: bronchial margin negative; vascular margin negative; parenchymal staple-line margin negative (14 mm); Lymphovascular invasion: not identified; Lymph nodes: 0 of 15 positive; stations examined: 6, 7, 8L, 9L, 11L; Pathologic stage (AJCC 8th ed.): pT1c pN0; Neoadjuvant therapy: none (untreated specimen).

GROSS DESCRIPTION:
The specimen is received as a left lobectomy of the lower lobe of lung and measures 15.7 x 8.3 x 4.1 cm. The pleural surface is smooth and glistening. On sectioning, a firm, tan-white mass is identified and measures 2.6 cm in greatest dimension. The surrounding lung parenchyma shows no additional nodules. Hilar lymph nodes are identified, and separately submitted lymph node stations are received. Representative sections are submitted in 13 cassettes.

MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION:
Sections show an invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma with a predominant acinar pattern. High-grade solid or micropapillary patterns comprise 30% of the tumor, consistent with IASLC grade 3. The tumor cells form glandular structures and display moderate nuclear atypia. The tumor measures 2.6 cm. The background lung shows mild anthracotic pigment. Visceral pleural invasion is not identified. There is no invasion of the chest wall or mediastinal structures. The bronchial margin, vascular margin, and parenchymal staple-line margin (14 mm) are negative. Lymphovascular invasion and spread through air spaces are not identified. Lymph nodes are 0 of 15 positive; stations examined are 6, 7, 8L, 9L, and 11L. Immunohistochemistry shows TTF-1 positivity and p40 negativity.

SURGICAL PATHOLOGY REPORT (SYNTHETIC; NOT A REAL PATIENT)
Patient: F, age band 50-59 | Report year: 2021

SPECIMEN: Colon (ascending colon), right hemicolectomy

FINAL DIAGNOSIS:
  Histologic type: Adenocarcinoma
  Histologic grade: G2, moderately differentiated
  Tumor size: 4.8 cm
  Depth of invasion: invades through the muscularis propria into pericolorectal soft tissue, 13 mm beyond the muscularis propria
  Margins: proximal margin negative (8.6 cm); distal margin negative (10.8 cm); radial (retroperitoneal) margin negative (7 mm)
  Lymphovascular invasion: not identified
  Perineural invasion: present
  Macroscopic tumor perforation: not identified
  Tumor deposits: not identified
  Lymph nodes: 8 of 32 positive
  Pathologic stage (AJCC 8th ed.): pT3 pN2b
  Neoadjuvant therapy: none (untreated specimen)

GROSS DESCRIPTION:
The specimen consists of a 24.0 cm segment of colon, identified as the ascending colon, submitted as a right hemicolectomy with attached mesentery and a 3.2 cm segment of terminal ileum. An annular, firm mass is present, measuring 4.8 cm in greatest dimension. The mass is located 8.6 cm from the closest margin, which is the proximal margin. On sectioning, the tumor appears to extend through the bowel wall into the pericolic fat. Lymph nodes are identified in the mesenteric fat. Representative sections are submitted in 25 cassettes.

MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION:
Sections demonstrate adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated (G2). The tumor cells form irregular glands exhibiting moderate nuclear atypia, with luminal necrosis, set within a desmoplastic stroma. A tubular adenoma is present adjacent to the tumor. The tumor invades through the muscularis propria into the pericolorectal soft tissue, extending 13 mm beyond the muscularis propria. The proximal margin is negative at 8.6 cm, the distal margin is negative at 10.8 cm, and the radial (retroperitoneal) margin is negative at 7 mm. Lymphovascular invasion is not identified. Perineural invasion is present. Macroscopic tumor perforation is not identified, and tumor deposits are not identified. Lymph nodes show carcinoma in 8 of 32 nodes examined. Mismatch repair immunohistochemistry demonstrates intact nuclear expression of MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6.
